title: Basic Approach to Kidney Disease and Renal Artery Stenosis

questions.q: The initial investigation of kidney disease pairs USG abdomen and renal function tests with:
questions.exp: Initial investigation: ultrasonography (USG) abdomen, renal function test (RFT) and urine analysis. (Book p748)

questions.q: For protein estimation in the initial urine analysis, the preferred test is:
questions.exp: Urine analysis: 24hr protein (preferred), albumin/creatinine, protein/creatinine. (Book p748)

questions.q: The RFT arm of the initial investigation measures:
opts: S. urea, S. creatinine, S. Na+ and S. K+
S. urea, S. uric acid, S. Ca2+ and S. Mg2+
S. creatinine, S. albumin, S. Na+ and S. K+
S. urea, S. creatinine, S. ALT and S. AST
questions.exp: RFT: S. urea, S. creatinine, S. Na+, S. K+. (Book p748)

questions.q: On the USG approach, a kidney size below which value points toward chronic kidney disease?
questions.exp: Look for: kidney size <8 cm. (Book p748)

questions.q: Kidneys larger than 10 cm with loss of corticomedullary differentiation are classically seen with:
questions.exp: >10 cm with loss of CMD with: DM, HIV, amyloidosis. (Book p748)

questions.q: Enlarged (>10 cm) kidneys with loss of CMD are listed for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Loss of CMD with >10 cm kidneys: DM, HIV, amyloidosis; vesicoureteral reflux belongs to the asymmetric-kidney note. (Book p748)

questions.q: Fill up: On the USG approach, seeing corticomedullary differentiation (CMD) places the patient in the ______ arm.
questions.exp: CMD present → CKD; absent → non-CKD. (Book p748)

questions.q: Match each normal-kidney USG structure with its echogenicity — 1) Cortex 2) Pyramids 3) Fat, calyx, sinus, vessels … A) Hyperechoic B) Isoechoic C) Hypoechoic
questions.exp: Isoechoic: cortex; hypoechoic: pyramids; hyperechoic: fat, calyx, sinus, vessels. (Book p748)

questions.q: Which statement about the USG approach is TRUE?
opts: USG abdomen is the most important investigation of the approach
Loss of CMD rules out chronic kidney disease
Kidneys of 8-10 cm always retain CMD
Absent CMD places the patient in the CKD arm
questions.exp: USG abdomen (most important); CMD present → CKD, absent → non-CKD; 8-10 cm loss of CMD is itself a CKD clue. (Book p748)

questions.q: The two end-point branches drawn for established CKD are:
questions.exp: CKD → hemodialysis / transplant. (Book p748)

questions.q: Before diagnosing CKD on USG one must rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis, whose clue on imaging is:
opts: Calyces becoming prominent and ureter seen
questions.exp: Rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis before diagnosing CKD; calyces becoming prominent and ureter seen. (Book p749)

questions.q: Match each tempo with its non-CKD category — 1) Hours to days 2) Days to weeks 3) Normal RFT with renal disease … A) Acute kidney injury (AKI) B) Rapidly progressive renal failure (RPRF) C) Nephrotic syn / RTA type I-II / asymptomatic urine abnormality
questions.exp: Hours to days → AKI; days to weeks → RPRF; normal RFT with renal disease → nephrotic syn, RTA I/II, asymptomatic urine abnormality. (Book p749)

questions.q: The AKI arm of the flowchart lists postrenal, ATN, AIN and:
opts: Pre-renal investigation with normal urine analysis
questions.exp: AKI: postrenal (B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis on USG), pre-renal (normal urine analysis), ATN, AIN. (Book p749)

questions.q: Which statement about the AKI arm is TRUE?
opts: The pre-renal category is expected to show a normal urine analysis
The postrenal category shows a normal USG
ATN and AIN are postrenal causes
B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis defines the pre-renal category
questions.exp: Pre-renal investigation: normal urine analysis; postrenal: B/L hydronephroureteronephrosis (USG). (Book p749)

questions.q: Rapidly progressive renal failure most commonly turns out to be:
questions.exp: RPRF → RPGN (m/c), diagnosed with biopsy; severe ATN and TMA are rare causes. (Book p749)

questions.q: All of the following appear under rapidly progressive renal failure in the flowchart EXCEPT:
questions.exp: RPRF: RPGN (m/c), severe ATN, TMA; nephrotic syndrome sits under normal RFT with renal disease. (Book p749)

questions.q: Match each item of the hypertensive-crisis branch with its label — 1) Renal artery stenosis 2) Thrombotic microangiopathy 3) Hypertensive crisis … A) Small vessel kidney disease B) Large vessel kidney disease C) Vascular cause
questions.exp: Hypertensive crisis: vascular cause; RAS = large vessel kidney disease; TMA = small vessel kidney disease. (Book p749)

questions.q: Normal RFT with renal disease includes nephrotic syndrome, asymptomatic urine abnormality and:
questions.exp: Normal RFT with renal disease: nephrotic syn, renal tubular acidosis type I/II, asymptomatic urine abnormality. (Book p749)

questions.q: Renal artery stenosis is also known as:
opts: Renovascular HTN (RVH) / renal artery occlusion disease (RAOD)
questions.exp: AKA renovascular HTN (RVH) / renal artery occlusion disease (RAOD). (Book p749)

questions.q: Left untreated, renal artery stenosis can progress to:
questions.exp: Can progress to CKD / ischemic nephropathy. (Book p749)

questions.q: Which vessel-size statement is TRUE as per the flowchart?
opts: TMA is a small vessel kidney disease while RAS is a large vessel kidney disease
TMA is a large vessel kidney disease while RAS is a small vessel kidney disease
Both TMA and RAS are small vessel diseases
Both TMA and RAS are large vessel diseases
questions.exp: RAS: large vessel kidney disease; TMA: small vessel kidney disease. (Book p749)

questions.q: Match each population with its most common cause of RAS — 1) Overall 2) Young population 3) Indian/Asian population … A) Takayasu arteritis B) Atherosclerosis C) Fibromuscular dysplasia
questions.exp: Overall: atherosclerosis; young population: fibromuscular dysplasia; Indian/Asian: Takayasu arteritis. (Book p750)

questions.q: In young males, the cause of RAS that involves the entire length of the renal artery with microaneurysms is:
questions.exp: Young males: polyarteritis nodosa – entire length renal artery – microaneurysm. (Book p750)

questions.q: Atherosclerotic RAS involves the proximal renal artery over 1-2 cm and becomes symptomatic beyond what occlusion?
questions.exp: Atherosclerosis: proximal renal artery (1-2 cm); symptomatic: >80% occlusion. (Book p750)

questions.q: Fill up: Fibromuscular dysplasia, the young-population cause, affects the ______ renal artery.
questions.exp: Fibromuscular dysplasia (arteriopathy): mid to distal renal artery. (Book p750)

questions.q: The female-to-male ratio written for Takayasu arteritis is:
questions.exp: Takayasu arteritis (F:M = 9:1), proximal renal artery. (Book p750)

questions.q: The types of RAS are explained by the Goldblatt:
questions.exp: Explain by Goldblatt: two kidney one clip model. (Book p750)

questions.q: The pathogenesis of unilateral RAS starts with the clue:
questions.exp: Unilateral RAS pathogenesis: asymmetric kidney size. (Book p750)

questions.q: The written vasoconstriction potency order is:
questions.exp: Vasoconstriction potency: urotension > endothelin > AT-II. (Book p750)

questions.q: The clinical feature and basic investigation picture of unilateral RAS are:
opts: Persistent HTN with RFT and urine analysis in the normal range
Persistent HTN with abnormal urine analysis
Flash pulmonary edema with raised S. creatinine
questions.exp: C/F: persistent HTN; basic investigation (RFT, urine analysis) normal range. (Book p750)

questions.q: In the affected kidney of unilateral RAS, the sequence after reduced RBF/perfusion is:
opts: Renin angiotensin system → ↑ aldosterone → ↑ AT-II → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ BP
questions.exp: Affected kidney: ↓ RBF/perfusion → (+) renin angiotensin → (+) ↑ aldosterone → ↑ AT-II ↑↑ → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ BP → HTN/HTN crisis. (Book p750)

questions.q: Fill up: In the normal kidney, ↑ renal interstitial hydrostatic pressure reduces reabsorption from the ______, producing pressure natriuresis.
questions.exp: Normal kidney: ↑ RIHP → ↓ reabsorption from PCT → ↑ excretion of Na+/H2O (pressure natriuresis theory). (Book p750)

questions.q: Which statement about the normal (contralateral) kidney in unilateral RAS is TRUE?
opts: It shows ↑ renal blood flow/medullary flow with ↑ RIHP
It shows ↓ renal blood flow and activated renin
It reabsorbs more sodium from the PCT
questions.exp: Normal kidney: ↑ RBF/medullary flow → ↑ RIHP → ↓ PCT reabsorption → ↑ Na+/H2O excretion. (Book p750)

questions.q: The book's note lists asymmetric kidney in vesicoureteral reflux and renal artery stenosis; it is NOT listed for:
questions.exp: Asymmetric kidney seen in: vesicoureteral reflux; renal artery stenosis. (Book p750)

questions.q: In the affected kidney, the doubly-raised AT-II produces:
opts: Profound vasoconstriction with rising blood pressure
questions.exp: ↑ Angiotensin II (AT-II) ↑↑ → profound vasoconstriction → ↑ blood pressure → HTN/HTN crisis. (Book p750)

questions.q: On USG the radiological clue for RAS is asymmetric kidney; the screening test is:
questions.exp: On USG: asymmetric kidney; screening test: renal doppler. (Book p751)

questions.q: The investigation of choice to confirm renal artery stenosis is:
opts: CT renal angio or MR angiography
questions.exp: IOC: CT renal angio or MR angiography (confirms the doppler screen). (Book p751)

questions.q: The drug of choice written for unilateral RAS is:
questions.exp: Treatment: ACE inhibitors / ARBs – (DOC). (Book p751)

questions.q: Percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty (PTRA) is offered only if the kidney size is above:
questions.exp: PTRA – only if kidney size > 8 cm. (Book p751)

questions.q: The prognosis written for bilateral RAS is:
opts: Responsive to PTRA alone without stenting
questions.exp: Bilateral RAS: poor prognosis. (Book p751)

questions.q: In bilateral RAS, loss of pressure natriuresis with ↓ RIHP leads to:
opts: ↑ Na+/H2O retention → intravascular volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema
Sustained renin activation without volume change
questions.exp: Loss of pressure natriuresis / ↓ RIHP → ↑ Na+/H2O retention → intravascular volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema (d/t intravascular edema). (Book p751)

questions.q: Which statement about the bilateral RAS diagram is TRUE?
opts: Intravascular volume overload feeds back negatively on the renin angiotensin system
The renin angiotensin system stays maximally stimulated without feedback
Pressure natriuresis is preserved in both kidneys
questions.exp: The (−) arrow shows intravascular volume overload inhibiting the renin angiotensin system. (Book p751)

questions.q: Recurrent flash pulmonary edema in bilateral RAS is treated with:
opts: B/L percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty with stenting
questions.exp: Rx: B/L percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty with stenting. (Book p751)

questions.q: For blood pressure control in bilateral RAS, the book lists diuretics as DOC while ACE inhibitors/ARBs are:
questions.exp: In BP: diuretics (DOC); ACE inhibitors / ARBs: C/I as they ↓ GFR. (Book p751)

questions.q: All of the following are listed in the bilateral RAS treatment block EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Listed: diuretics (DOC), stop smoking, start statins; ACEi/ARBs are C/I. (Book p751)

questions.q: The book's caution while interpreting flash pulmonary edema in this context is:
opts: Every pulmonary edema is cardiac unless proven otherwise
Every pulmonary edema is renal unless proven otherwise
Flash pulmonary edema excludes cardiac disease
Pulmonary edema never occurs in bilateral RAS
questions.exp: Note: every pulmonary edema is cardiac unless proven otherwise. (Book p752)

questions.q: The screening test named on this page is renal artery stenosis colour doppler ultrasound (CDU); its characteristic waveform clue is the:
questions.exp: Screening test: RAS colour doppler ultrasound (CDU); look for parvus tardus pattern. (Book p752)

questions.q: On CDU, a resistivity index (RI) at or above which value points to parenchymal disease (CKD)?
questions.exp: RI ≥ 0.8 → parenchymal disease: CKD. (Book p752)

questions.q: With RI < 0.8, the stenosis criteria that route the patient to CT/MR renal angiography are:
opts: Peak systolic velocity > 180 cm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.05
Peak systolic velocity > 100 cm/s OR RAR > 2.5 OR ΔRI > 0.01
Peak systolic velocity > 250 cm/s OR RAR > 5 OR ΔRI > 0.1
Peak systolic velocity > 180 mm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.5
questions.exp: RI < 0.8 with PSV > 180 cm/s OR RAR > 3.5 OR ΔRI > 0.05 → CT/MR renal angiography (IOC). (Book p752)

questions.q: All of the following are CDU look-for criteria of RAS EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The book's velocity criterion is peak systolic velocity > 180 cm/s, not 80 cm/s. (Book p752)

questions.q: The IOC after a positive screen is CT/MR renal angiography; the gold standard that is both diagnostic and therapeutic is:
questions.exp: Conventional angiograph (gold standard): diagnostic and therapeutic. (Book p752)

questions.q: Which statement about fibromuscular dysplasia is TRUE?
opts: It is a non-atherosclerotic, non-inflammatory arteriopathy most common in young girls
It is an atherosclerotic disease of elderly males
It is an inflammatory vasculitis of the proximal aorta
questions.exp: Non atherosclerotic/non inflammatory arteriopathy; incident: m/c in young girls. (Book p752)

questions.q: The pathology of fibromuscular dysplasia is medial fibroplasia in the tunica media of the:
questions.exp: Involves middle to distal renal artery: medial fibroplasia in tunica media. (Book p752)

questions.q: Fibromuscular dysplasia is bilateral in the renal arteries in 25% of cases; the other 25% involve:
questions.exp: 25% B/L renal artery, 25% involves cerebral vessels. (Book p752)

questions.q: The angiographic feature illustrated for medial fibromuscular dysplasia is the:
questions.exp: The "string of beads" feature in medial fibromuscular dysplasia. (Book p752)

questions.q: The treatment of choice for fibromuscular dysplasia, carrying a good prognosis, is:
questions.exp: Treatment: PTRA (good prognosis). (Book p752)

units.title: Initial investigation & USG approach
units.guide: The initial triad (USG abdomen, RFT with urea/creatinine/Na+/K+, urine analysis with preferred 24hr protein), the size/CMD algorithm (<8 cm, 8-10 cm loss of CMD, >10 cm loss of CMD in DM/HIV/amyloidosis), normal-kidney echogenicity and the CKD end-points.

units.title: CKD mimics & the AKI arm
units.guide: Rule out hydronephroureteronephrosis before labelling CKD, then the tempo-based non-CKD split: hours-days AKI (postrenal/pre-renal/ATN/AIN) with the prerenal normal-urine clue.

units.title: RPRF, vascular causes & RAS introduction
units.guide: Days-weeks RPRF (RPGN m/c by biopsy; severe ATN/TMA rare), the hypertensive-crisis vascular branch (RAS large-vessel vs TMA small-vessel), the normal-RFT trio, and RAS aliases and its progression to CKD/ischemic nephropathy.

units.title: RAS: most common causes & Goldblatt model
units.guide: Cause-by-population table (atherosclerosis proximal 1-2 cm >80% occlusion; FMD mid-distal; Takayasu F:M 9:1 proximal; PAN young males entire length with microaneurysm), the two-kidney-one-clip model and the asymmetric-kidney entry point.

units.title: Unilateral RAS pathogenesis
units.guide: Both limbs of the unilateral diagram: affected kidney (↓RBF → renin → aldosterone → AT-II ↑↑ → vasoconstriction → HTN) vs normal kidney (↑RBF/↑RIHP → ↓PCT reabsorption → pressure natriuresis), plus vasoconstrictor potency and the persistent-HTN/normal-basic-Ix picture.

units.title: RAS investigations & unilateral treatment
units.guide: USG asymmetric kidney → renal doppler screen → CT/MR angiography IOC; ACEi/ARBs as DOC and PTRA only when the kidney is >8 cm.

units.title: Bilateral RAS: pathogenesis & treatment
units.guide: Poor prognosis; loss of pressure natriuresis/↓RIHP → Na+/H2O retention → volume overload → flash pulmonary edema with (−) renin feedback; B/L PTRA with stenting; diuretics DOC with ACEi/ARBs C/I; stop smoking and statins.

units.title: CDU screening values & fibromuscular dysplasia
units.guide: CDU with parvus tardus, RI ≥ 0.8 → CKD vs RI < 0.8 with PSV >180 cm/s / RAR >3.5 / ΔRI >0.05 → CT/MR IOC and conventional angiography gold standard; FMD's young-girl epidemiology, medial fibroplasia, 25% bilateral/25% cerebral, string-of-beads and PTRA.
